the-four-names.description: Drew Breunig named context poisoning, distraction, confusion and clash in June 2025: poisoning is an error that gets saved and reused, distraction a long history that steers the model, confusion superfluous material such as surplus tools, clash conflicting material in the window [1].

credit-and-limit.description: the IBM Technology video presents the same four. The taxonomy is a practitioner blog post and a failure can fit more than one mode [1].

numbers-for-confusion-and-clash.description: on the Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard every model does worse with more than one tool, a quantized Llama 3.1 8b failed with 46 tools and succeeded with 19; piecemeal prompts cut scores by 39% on average [1].

breunig-how-long-contexts-fail.title: Drew Breunig, How Long Contexts Fail

junk-drawer-meeting-two-bosses.title: Junk drawer, meeting, two bosses
junk-drawer-meeting-two-bosses.script: Everyday comparisons first, because the technical names come later. Imagine a recipe with one wrong fact in it: you then cook from it every time. Imagine a long meeting that forgets its own decision. Imagine a junk drawer of keys, where you cannot find the one you need. Imagine two bosses with opposite instructions. Keep those four in mind; now we put them on the bench.

static-row.title: Static row
static-row.script: Now the same four at the bench, on the static side, set up before the shift. A wrong screw size on the instruction sheet. A binder with every bike model, when you build one. Fifty near-identical wrenches. Old and new instruction sheets pinned up side by side.

dynamic-row.title: Dynamic row
dynamic-row.script: The same four arrive during the shift too. A mislabeled box of screws, colleagues dropping by with questions, ten crates of similar parts, someone shouting rush it, while the sheet on the wall says check every piece. The names for these are poisoning, distraction, confusion and clash. The names are the label, and the bench is the picture.

more-context-worse-result.title: More context, worse result
more-context-worse-result.script: More is not safer. A fuller bench can be a worse bench. Adding one more document to be on the safe side is exactly how most of these messes begin.
